newsitem.title: UK: Creator of BBC's Archers dies at 92.
newsitem.headline: Creator of BBC's Archers dies at 92.

text.p: Godfrey Baseley, who dreamed up the Archers, the world's longest-running radio serial, has died at the age of 92, the BBC said on Sunday.
Baseley died in a hospital in Bromsgrove, central England, after a long illness, the BBC said.

Having proposed a daily radio programme based on farming to help farmers modernise production after World War II, Baseley came up with the tale of Dan and Doris Archer and their family at Brookfield Farm in the mythical village of Ambridge.
Baseley edited the saga for 22 years. After more than 46 years on air, it regularly attracts nearly four million fans in Britain as well as in continental Europe.
"Godfrey Baseley created a programme that has become a national institution," Archers' current editor Vanessa Whitburn said in a statement.
"Millions of listeners are indebted to him for the pleasure it has given them over the past 46 years. We have lost a gifted broadcaster who was also a friend."
Baseley's wife Betty died eight years ago. The couple had two daughters, Jane and Helen,six grandchildren and nine great grandchildren.
